verdict: No figure in the five docs contradicts its cited source. All E1 table values, the E2/E3/E4 counts and the E5 description match. The docs' main disclaimers are present: not MPC, real loop missing, A/B noncausal, FIFO/throughput/fairness gaps, no SLO guarantee and a portability gap. Ten wording/protocol findings remain. One is high: the P0 gate has no evaluation-vs-development separation (leakage). Five are medium: reproducibility wording, reproduction-command scope and pinning, a CPU-vs-native and cleanup bullet, E2 scope/shadow wording, and version attribution. Four are low.

findings.issue: The docs never name the scored P0 workload or require it to be disjoint from the data used to fit the predictor, build scenario panels, select Fixed or tune MPC/OneMove. The only collected long workload is the Azure development trace, which was used for A/B identification and model training. Replaying that trace for the comparison would score MPC, and any baseline tuned on the trace, in-sample. A scenario panel built from A/B captures of the same trace would carry near-copies of the evaluation's own future arrivals: privileged future information that interview_defense.md:56 forbids but that no gate operationally excludes. In addition, A/B are time-varying schedules, not Fixed runs, so 'development-selected Fixed' needs a declared selection procedure.
